$comment: Tooling reviews name the dependency path, input boundary, reachable code and expiry. Records with advisoryIds cover only those identifiers and reject unlisted findings. The four existing records without identifiers retain legacy package-wide scope and require individual advisory assessment under S16. See docs/privacy-security.md.

reviewed.advisory: image-size ICNS/JXL/HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
reviewed.justification: Metro measures image assets while bundling the native app on a developer machine. It never runs on a player device and is not part of the web runtime or the shipped iOS/Android bundle. The parser only sees asset files committed to this repository, so there is no untrusted input path.
reviewed.fixNotes: Every published image-size version is in the vulnerable range, so no upgrade resolves this. npm proposes downgrading expo 57 to 53, a semver-major downgrade that would break the verified native Link build. Re-check for a patched image-size release at the review date.

reviewed.advisory: uuid missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when buf is provided
reviewed.justification: The xcode package rewrites Xcode project files during iOS prebuild on a developer machine. It calls only uuid.v4(); the advisory concerns v3/v5/v6 called with an explicit buf argument, so the vulnerable code path is not reached.
reviewed.fixNotes: Patched in uuid >= 11.1.1, but the fix lives inside a transitive dependency of Expo's own tooling. Forcing an override into xcode's internals risks breaking iOS project generation for an unreachable code path. Adopt it when Expo updates xcode upstream.

reviewed.advisory: xmldom: XML fragment injection via invalid EntityReference.nodeName during requireWellFormed serialization
reviewed.path: @101/controller-native > expo > @expo/cli > @expo/plist > @xmldom/xmldom, and @101/controller-native > expo > @expo/cli > @expo/config-plugins > xcode > simple-plist > plist > @xmldom/xmldom
reviewed.justification: Both paths are Expo prebuild tooling that runs on a developer machine: @expo/plist and simple-plist read and rewrite Info.plist and entitlements while generating the iOS project. Neither ships in the web runtime or in the built iOS/Android bundle. The only XML they serialize is this repository's own generated app configuration, so no attacker-controlled document reaches the vulnerable path.
reviewed.fixNotes: Patched above 0.9.11, but both copies are pinned inside Expo's own CLI dependency tree. Forcing an override into plist generation risks breaking iOS prebuild for a path that only ever sees our own files. Adopt when Expo updates @expo/plist and xcode upstream.

reviewed.advisory: fast-uri host confusion and SSRF via IDN canonicalization, IPv6 normalization and percent-decoding
reviewed.path: @101/controller-native > expo > @expo/cli > @expo/router-server > react-server-dom-webpack > webpack > schema-utils > ajv-formats > ajv > fast-uri
reviewed.justification: ajv uses fast-uri to resolve $ref URIs while validating webpack loader and plugin option schemas during bundling on a developer machine. The URIs it parses come from webpack's own schema files, not from the network or from user input, and none of this runs on a player device or in the shipped bundle. The SSRF and host-confusion classes require attacker-controlled URIs, which this path does not have.
reviewed.fixNotes: Patched above 3.1.5. It sits four levels inside Expo's router-server tooling; an override would pin a transitive dependency of webpack's schema validator. Adopt when ajv or webpack updates upstream, and re-check at the review date.

reviewed.advisory: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm: stack exhaustion through deeply nested patterns
reviewed.path: @101/controller-native > expo > @expo/metro-file-map > micromatch > braces; source build/lint > fast-glob > micromatch > braces
reviewed.justification: The installed recursive parser is affected. In the supported callers, Metro constructs watcher patterns from fixed strings and executable developer configuration; fast-glob patterns come from developer source AST or lint configuration. Filenames are matching inputs, not patterns. These inputs already belong to the developer who executes the build/configuration, so the claimed lower-trust pattern-to-process boundary is absent. This review covers the named advisory and current caller paths only; accepting lower-trust patterns requires a fresh assessment.
reviewed.fixNotes: No upstream patched version is listed. Do not downgrade Expo 57 to the unrelated major version suggested by npm. Reassess upstream fixes and pattern provenance at review.

reviewed.advisory: GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv: extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements during RSA verification
reviewed.justification: The affected verifier is installed, but Expo uses it to verify signatures it just generated with the local private key, or to validate an operator-supplied self-signed certificate that must match the provided private key. The iOS keychain path parses certificates without verifying attacker signatures. Current app configuration has neither EAS nor update code-signing certificates; the SDK builder permits only selected @101 dependencies. No supported caller exposes the dependency's certificate-issuing server API or accepts an attacker-supplied RSA signature. This review is advisory-specific; new certificate/signature inputs require reassessment.
reviewed.fixNotes: No upstream patched version is listed. Preserve Expo 57; reassess upstream fixes and any lower-trust signature or certificate API at review.
